claims.text: Factory Router's September 2026 production update reported that routed sessions cost 63% less in aggregate than the same workload at published frontier-model rates.

Factory Router reached 99% of Claude Opus 4.7's Terminal-Bench 2 pass rate and 96% on Legacy-Bench, choosing an efficient model when it can complete the task reliably and escalating to a stronger model when needed.
Among Factory Router sessions from Sep. 5–18, 84% saved at least 50%, and median per-session savings were 72.5%.

Factory Private (private preview, announced 2026-09-18) offers two deployment models: Factory Managed keeps the control plane hosted while Droids run on developer machines, CI/CD infrastructure or managed Droid Computers, and Factory Private places some or all infrastructure in the customer's VPC with sandbox execution through OpenCompute and customer IAM/network/security controls.
Factory said the NVIDIA Nemotron research team used Factory Private for post-training, evaluation and optimization while keeping code, models and IP in its own infrastructure.

Orq's September 2026 explainer describes a Software Factory as shared infrastructure around coding agents (workflow-specific context and skills, agent runtime/model/harness, execution environments, controls, observability and run evidence) that feeds a pull request into existing CI/CD rather than replacing source control or delivery.
Orq warned that stronger agents can follow dependencies into work nobody intended to delegate, making workflow boundaries and scope more important as capability improves.

Factory Automations became generally available on 2026-09-30 as a four-part workflow of trigger, instructions, model/reasoning level and computer, with triggers from schedules, Slack, GitHub or webhooks and runs under a user identity or service account with inspectable sessions, event history, seven-day success rate and failure notifications.

Factory reported that 30% of code-review automation runs used an open-weight model, and that among enterprise users in the prior 30 days 52% used automated code review, 48% security review and 35% AutoWiki, with session volume up 51% month over month.
Factory's own automations had median incident acknowledgement of 20 seconds and resolution of 6 minutes, reviewed 99.5% of mergeable PRs, and had 81% of comments resolved by engineers.

Factory's Environments announcement (2026-10-12) defines the sandbox as a reusable prebuilt definition of repositories, tools and dependencies, with images built ahead of time, rebuilt every few hours and promoted only after validation; automations start from the latest validated build.
Factory Environments let administrators centrally restrict reachable hosts, shell commands, approvals, Connectors and Skills, and a blocked command is stopped before execution.
Factory reported that most enterprise customers start at Agent Readiness level 2/5 and that its long-running Missions work best at level 4 or above.

Factory's OpenCompute private preview (2026-10-14) separates agent-sandbox fleet lifecycle from the underlying compute provider: a self-hosted service in the customer's environment connects outbound to Factory over TLS WebSockets, and a Go control plane records desired and observed state in local Postgres with a reconciler that retries provisioning.

OpenCompute uses standalone gRPC drivers for provider-specific operations, with required Core and optional Suspend/Snapshot/Fork conformance profiles and black-box tests that reject unsupported requests before durable state changes.
Factory said its first bespoke on-prem OpenCompute deployment took six weeks from prototype to first deployment and two days on site after the initial driver was built.

Microsoft's 2026-09-25 Copilot announcement added Code, which runs in a sandboxed environment that can be hosted inside the tenant, and Autopilot, a persistent proactive agent with its own identity, memory, computer and workspace governed by permissions, audit and organizational controls.
Microsoft said Copilot's Auto routing weighs accuracy, speed and cost per request, and that long-running Code and Autopilot use usage-based billing.

AWS's Deep Insight reference system uses eight specialized agents (Coordinator, Planner, Plan Reviewer, Supervisor, Coder, Validator, Reporter, Tracker), with a Strands Graph defining order and human-in-the-loop branching and role-specific models (Haiku for routing, Opus for planning, Sonnet for execution).

AWS reported selective prompt caching can cut repeated input-token costs by up to 90%, and an LG Electronics system using the same pattern reduced an analysis from three days to 30 minutes (288x); AWS also warned container isolation alone does not stop prompt injection in uploaded data.

The CRBugBench paper (2026-10-09; 1,800 tasks across 98 open-source repositories, two industry repositories and five languages) found the best agent caught 79.6% of pre-merge and 64.2% of post-merge bugs in its top five comments, with performance falling by up to 25.5% on proprietary repositories and agents missing more than 20% of human-found bugs.

CRBugBench found agents executed code in only 9.7% of the best model's turns; multi-agent review improved performance 4.7% at 5.55x cost, and higher reasoning raised performance from 36% to 57% at 23.22x cost; the authors recommend human-in-the-loop review.

The Instant Software Factories paper (2026-10-26) reported that in its CLI factory, about 30 scheduled agents raised daily merges 15x during rollout and filed 95% of new issues, but at least 5.6% of issues marked fixed were later incorrect, seven incorrect fixes shipped unrepaired, and the other factory's validation harness returned no verdict in 28% of reruns.

Google's Project Chrysalis (2026-10-22), a research reference architecture and demo rather than a disclosed production deployment, reported in simulation time-to-first-mitigation of 1.8 seconds versus 15–45 minutes and P99 latency falling from 519.8 ms to 18.2 ms, with permanent topology changes requiring dual-custody SRE approval.

Factory's Droid 1.0 (2026-10-29) made programmatic tool calling the default, with a sandboxed JavaScript Script running tool calls; it reported 15% lower cost on Claude Opus 5.5 and a 5,384-job CI sweep completed in two requests with under 0.1% of tool results reaching model context.
